'''''Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia''''' is a reference book from [[Dorling Kindersley]]. Authored by [[Adam Bray]], [[Cole Horton]], and [[Tricia Barr]], the book was released on [[April 4]], [[2017]]. The 200-page title features thousands of images with descriptions of various features from the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] grouped by topics. [[Leland Chee]], member of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] and Keeper of the  [[Holocron continuity database]], commented that "[this book] maybe the closest we'll ever get to doing an actual Holocron book."<ref name="HolocronKeeper">{{Twitter|HolocronKeeper|status/807076395792809984|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=This maybe the closest we'll ever get to doing an actual Holocron book.|archivedate=20190722071502|nolive=1}}</ref>

==Publisher's summary==
''Covering more than 2,500 characters, creatures, planets, vehicles, Droids™, weapons, technology, and more from the Star Wars™ universe, this visual tour is the ultimate compendium for the epic saga and beyond.''

''With a full history of the galactic politics, the Jedi Council, and the Empire, Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia walks fans through the entire timeline of Star Wars. Galleries of images and information on every page, including lightsabers, languages, clothing, and more, are showcased with fascinating facts and trivia. See the blasters of Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope™, look at the stormtroopers of Star Wars: The Force Awakens™, and study the geography of Rogue One: A Star Wars Story™.''

''Discover the food, architecture, transportation, and more from this galaxy far, far away. Each section of the book focuses on different topics to dedicate special attention and detail to every part of the universe, no matter how small. From the planets in the outer rim to Padmé's bridal wear, nothing is missed.''

''A celebration of all things Star Wars, this visual museum is the perfect addition to any fan's bookshelf.''

==Development==
{{Quote|The key to inventing new ''Star Wars'' information is to come up with things that sound natural and don't stick out like a sore thumb. I like to reference things that are already in ''Star Wars'' tradition — especially something obscure or meaningful to hardcore fans. Everyone loves an Easter egg, so I hide those in the text where I can. As a writer you never know how much of these things will survive the editing process or Story Group approval, so you can't be precious about these things.|Co-author Adam Bray|<ref name="SWcom">{{SW|url=news/7-things-you-didnt-know-about-star-wars-the-visual-encyclopedia|text=7 Things You Didn't Know About ''Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia''|nolive=1}}</ref>}}
''Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia'' was initiated by [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|British]] publisher [[Dorling Kindersley]] and the three authors [[Adam Bray]], [[Cole Horton]] and [[Tricia Barr]] were introduced to each other at [[Celebration Europe (2016)|Celebration Europe]]<ref name="SWcom" /> in the summer of [[2016]].<ref name="Tickets Page">{{Celebration|url=Tickets/Buy-Tickets|text=Europe Tickets|celebration=Celebration Europe|nolive=1}}</ref> The authors each designed two-page sections – or "spreads" – about specific topics they chose. All pages later were edited by DK and the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]]. The images for pages were often compiled by the editors and designers in advance of the writing process. The ''Visual Encyclopedia'' is also notable for being one of the firsts of the style of ''Star Wars'' books to include information from both all of the canon films and animated series instead of only one of the two.<ref name="SWcom" />

Bray worked on the pages for animal and [[plant]] [[species]] for which he was inspired by the creature work of [[Terryl Whitlatch]] and tried to re-canonize [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] elements from his work. Horton worked on the information for [[astromech droid]]s and tried to use the names for parts used by the [[R2-D2 Builders Club]] if multiple names had been used inconsistently in past works. Hourton also worked on the pages about [[Foodstuff|food]] and looked through the various recent novels for information and found that [[Chuck Wendig]]'s ''[[Star Wars: The Aftermath Trilogy|Aftermath Trilogy]]'' included the most references to ood. Barr worked on the information about the Royal Outfits of [[Naboo]] and [[Alderaan]] together with [[Natalie Edwards]] from DK and used ''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]'' by [[Trisha Biggar]] and the ''Star Wars'' and the Power of Costume Exhibit for references. Bray said that most of his work was spent scouring books and online ressources to look if things had already been named. He also sometimes had to make decisions when encountering conflicting information, like or pieces of technology which had animation assets had been reused for different purposes. Barr reflected that the book tried to compile existing information, but they tried to not unnessarily tie the hands of future authors in the process.<ref name="SWcom" />

The final credits for the book are Adam Bray, Cole Horton and Tricia Barr as authors; [[Ruth Amos]] as overall project editor, [[Toby Truphet]] as the project art editor, [[Elizabeth Dowsett]] as senior editor; [[Matt Jones]], [[Natalie Edwards]], [[David Fentiman]] and [[Emma Grange]] as additional editors; additional art design by [[Abi Wright]] and [[Owen Bennett]]; [[Marc Staples]] as pre-production producer, [[Mary Slater]] as senior producer, [[Sadie Smith]] as managing editor, [[Ron Stobbart]] as managing art editor, [[Lisa Lanzarini]] as art director, [[Julie Ferris]] as publisher and [[Simon Beecroft]] as publishing director. Additional thanks were given to "[[Frank Parisi]], [[Leland Chee]], [[Matt Martin]], [[Pablo Hidalgo]], and [[Michael Siglain]] at Lucasfilm; Chelsea Alon at Disney Publishing; [[Dennis Muren]] and [[Courtney Miller]] at [[Industrial Light & Magic|ILM]]; [[Jason Fry]] for his expertise and help on the map of the galaxy and planet spreads; Lynne Moulding and Chris Gould for design assistance; Ben Davies, Lauren Nesworthy, Lisa Stock, and Eleanor Rose for editorial assistance; Lindsay Kent for proofreading; and Vanessa Bird for the index."<ref name="VE" />

Matt Marin of the Story Group joked on social media that the book would "put me out of a job".<ref name="HolocronKeeper" />
